svg.text: picowallet perfboard: 18650 through a switch and a 1N5817 into VSYS, USB stays plugged for programming, ATECC608 on I2C0
Pico 2 W seen from the top, USB up. Everything solders to the pin tails under the board. Numbers are physical header pins. A dot joins wires.
the one wire that crosses to the right column
Those colors are the Adafruit STEMMA QT convention. A cable from a kit
may differ: map each bare wire to the VIN / GND / SDA / SCL pads with a
meter (continuity) before anything is powered. Swapped VIN and GND puts
3.3 V on the chip's ground; swapped SDA and SCL is harmless.
a bare cell has no over-discharge or short
protection: protected cell, or a holder + DW01 board
no charger at all: see wiring-battery-atecc-swap.svg
cell -, divider and module ground: one wire to the Pico's GND
Why the cell and USB can be in at the same time
the Pico's own Schottky puts ~4.7 V on VSYS, above any cell,
so the 1N5817 is reverse-biased. No USB current reaches the cell:
it is never charged through this circuit, and it never pushes
VSYS = Vcell - ~0.35 V, about 2.7 to 3.9 V. The buck-boost
holds 3.3 V down to VSYS 1.8 V, so the whole cell is usable.
the higher source wins, the other diode just blocks. That is
the documented Pico pattern; unplugging USB does not reboot.
the cell is isolated and the divider reads 0 V; nothing
back-feeds an unpowered Pico through GP28.
out of the wallet in a charger, or the TP4056 + DW01 module
through its own port. A TP4056 without the DW01 pads has no
protection: skip it. Never charge through the Pico's USB.
Switch the wallet OFF while it charges: a load on OUT+ keeps the
TP4056 from ever seeing the end of charge.
Before the cell goes in (meter, USB unplugged, switch OFF)
[ ] diode mode across the 1N5817: 0.2 to 0.35 V one way, open the
other way; the band sits at the pin 39 end
[ ] VSYS (39) to GND is not a short
[ ] the holder's + lead is open to everything with the switch OFF
[ ] VIN -> 36, GND -> 8, SDA -> 6, SCL -> 7; no continuity 36 to 8
[ ] then cell in, switch ON, USB out: the screen comes up and the
home screen shows the cell voltage
The diode backwards is the only way to get it wrong, and it is harmless:
the cell just never powers the Pico. Never wire the cell to VBUS (40)
or 3V3 OUT (36): VSYS (39) is the only input for the cell.
